# Other Blooded
## Honor code breaches The Honor Code is very strict and unforgiving. If you see a breach, do your best to make the offender desist. If they refuse and don't self-destruct, challenge them to an honor duel.
[color=#ff0000][bold]Murdering a fellow Yautja outside an honor duel is the worst possible crime[/bold][/color], and will result in disciplinary action against your whitelist. Accidents in spars are excused.
## Respect for elites, elders and ancients Hunters are expected to show respect to their superiors, be they elites, elders or ancients, even from other clans. How this looks can vary from character to character, but do not disrespect superiors to bait honor duels.
## Honor duels Yautja may challenge another blooded Yautja, or a human they deem worthy, to an honor duel. Honor duels are to the death, with some rules: - The challenging Yautja chooses the rules of the duel, such as the weapons and gear either party may use, and whether humans may use ranged weapons. - A Yautja on Yautja honor duel requires a major incident between the two, such as the theft of a trophy or grave insults. - Human victors may be given a trophy from the ship by the other Yautja, or one of the fallen Yautja's gear pieces.
## Cooperation Yautja must hunt alone. With consent from the other Yautja, the only things you may do as a group are: - Dispatching dishonorable prey. - Gear and body retrieval. - Hunting abominations and aberrations. - Defending lodges.
The only cases where Yautja are obliged to work together are killing abominations and aberrations, and facility purges.
## Death of yourself and of other Yautja Dying in combat is one of the greatest deaths a Yautja could ask for, but dying by a bracer's self-destruct is an even greater honor. If a Yautja is about to die, they must try to self-destruct.
- Once you commit to self-destructing, you must go through with it unless you have a very good reason to cancel. - Self-destructing and then cancelling to scare away enemies is extremely dishonorable. - While self-destructing, you cannot use any weapons or try to keep xenos or humans within the blast radius. - You will never be disciplined for not self-destructing, but you should make every attempt to do so within the bounds of the Honor Code.
You may self-destruct fallen Yautja as you see fit, provided they are not in the FOB or the hive. Do not throw the body as a weapon after triggering the self-destruct, and the same rule about keeping humans or threats within the blast radius applies.
Yautja should make every effort to avoid self-destructing in the FOB or the hive. If it is completely unavoidable you may do so, but you may be reported and should be prepared to defend your actions.
